A day about eating candy, wearing fun costumes and watching a popular genre of movies is more popular than a day commemorating a failed terrorist attack in a sectarian conflict? Especially between two religious groups that have shrinking memberships in the population.

Let me shake my hand at the clouds and swear my undying loyalty to how much better than me and innately deserving of rulership a specific family dynasty is.

But if we aren't homogenized, how can we market the Halloween special episodes, the Halloween merch, the Halloween hamburger menu and the Halloween latte?

Thanksgiving seems to be a harder sell.

Like many holidays, it can be overdone. But kids have fun; and flirty costumes aren’t required. The last time that I took my daughter out before she aged out of the tradition, we went as plague doctor and victim. We worked for weeks on the setup. It was a lot of fun for the family.

The pseudo-holiday I object to is “Black Friday” which shouldn’t be a thing here in Canada, but it is now. It’s ridiculous. Our Thanksgiving is in October, not November. And given the official anti-Canadian policy in the U.S. federal government, I couldn’t be any less interested in U.S. marketing exports.

Totally crass. Who wants an excuse to have fun, have kids and co-eds dress up in flirty clothing, and eat candy?

Who would EVER think that's a good idea.

America sucks.

I personally like that people can take a day to be silly and even dress up and try things they never have before. If you don't like the commercialization of it, don't play into it. Getting some makeup and a few accessories, and making lasting memories with friends and family only sound positive to me. Perhaps this is why it is more popular now than Easter; as anyone can participate sans religion.
In some places in Asia, Halloween is commodified and appropriated to voice dissent. It was crazy to see. It is now crushed (some times literally rip)

Halloween was explicitly banned in New England for most of our history.

I believe the Irish brought the tradition here much later and then American consumerism came along turning into what it has become

Personally I'm over it, candy is bad for you anyway.

It’s a memetic spread. Businesses latched on and started selling accessories, orange pumpkins et c.

Christmas trees and Santa Claus came first.
Fun is cool actually. That’s my hot take

Halloween is at its best when it's a maker's holiday. Handmade costumes and decorations. Let that freak flag fly. I give full-sized candy bars to all the kids who make their own costumes. The ones who bought "generic soldier" get a Laffy Taffy or some other boring candy with no effort, just like their costumes.

technically, American imported it from Celtic traditions and the source is much closer to home for UK
